newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade on Monday, dealers said.
They said most people were reluctant to open or hold new positions and were sitting on the sidelines, due mainly to an absence of fresh incentives.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning except for some light activity at the short end. Some people are waiting for fresh clues to market direction from Tuesday's release of the (U.S. June) consumer confidence index," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact here unless the numbers are way off market expectations," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Monday/Tuesday rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.
Tuesday/Wednesday and week-fixed were unchanged from last Friday's common 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8, nine-months unchanged at 5-15/16 5-13/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/15 5-15/16 percent.
